correctness.rationale: For a total dominating set \(D\), each coordinate hyperplane \(H_i\) is covered by the proper subspaces \(H_i\cap d^\perp\). If \(|D|\le q\), the finite-vector-space covering lemma forces one \(d^\perp\) to contain \(H_i\), hence \(d\) is on the \(i\)-th coordinate axis; doing this for every \(i\) gives \(|D|\ge n\). This proves the lower bound \(\min\{n,q+1\}\). The coordinate basis realizes \(n\); beyond the threshold, projective representatives of a suitable two-plane realize \(q+1\). Pairing arguments give the least even size: the basis construction handles \(n\le q+1\), anisotropic two-planes handle odd \(q\) beyond the threshold, a totally isotropic two-plane plus one extra vector handles even \(q,n\ge5\), and \((q,n)=(2,4)\) has the explicit four-vertex witness. Fresh exhaustive calculations for \((q,n)=(2,3),(2,4),(3,3),(3,4)\) reproduced both formulas; these finite cases are corroborative only.

evidence: The ambient total graph has \(\gamma_t=q+1\) and a parity-dependent paired value, whereas the zero-divisor induced graph has \(\gamma_t=n\) below the threshold.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The ambient theorem is highly relevant but does not dominate the induced-subgraph result.

originality.rationale: Badawi and Abdulla–Badawi define and structurally analyze these dot-product graphs; the latter full paper treats finite-field structure in the two-factor case. Saleh–Megahed studies ordinary domination for total dot-product graphs over residue rings, not total or paired domination of the zero-divisor induced graph. A published SCOPE theorem gives total/paired domination for the ambient finite-field total dot-product graph, with \(q+1\) as the total-domination value; it does not imply the zero-divisor threshold because the induced graph has the strictly smaller value \(n\) when \(n<q+1\), and domination is not inherited monotonically from the ambient graph. No inspected source covers the two-regime formula.
residual_risks: An unindexed finite-geometry treatment could phrase the same problem as covering the union of coordinate hyperplanes by orthogonal hyperplanes; no such theorem was located.

value.rationale: The result identifies a sharp and geometrically natural competition between the \(n\) coordinate hyperplanes defining the zero-divisor locus and the \(q+1\) hyperplanes of a projective line. Exact total and paired domination are standard strengthened domination invariants, and the dimension-field transition is a meaningful structural boundary rather than an arbitrary finite computation.
residual_risks: No classification of all minimum dominating sets is claimed.

final_claim: For every prime power \(q\) and \(n\ge3\), the zero-divisor dot product graph on nonzero vectors of \(\mathbb F_q^n\) having at least one zero coordinate satisfies \(\gamma_t=\min\{n,q+1\}\) and \(\gamma_{\mathrm{pr}}=2\lceil\min\{n,q+1\}/2\rceil\).
scientific_limitations: The theorem uses the standard dot product over a finite field and does not extend automatically to chain rings or degenerate bilinear forms.
The result determines minimum cardinalities, not every minimum set.
